newsitem.title: INDIA: India MICO jumps on budget tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: India MICO jumps on budget tax cuts.

text.p: Shares of auto components maker MICO surged 200 rupees or 3.4 percent to 6,100 in early trade on the Bombay bourse on Saturday, traders said.
They said MICO was a leading beneficiary of wide-ranging tax cuts announced in India's federal budget on Friday.
MICO shares had soared 427 rupees, or nearly eight percent, to 5,900 in post-budget trade on Friday.
In the federal budget for 1997/98 (April-March), Finance Minister P. Chidambaram swept away a corporate surcharge and cut corporate tax rates across the board.

The finance minister said he was abolishing a 7.5 percent surcharge on corporate profits. He also lowered a tax on domestic firms' profits to 35 percent from 40 percent, and on foreign firms' profits to 48 percent from 55 percent.
He said the reduction in corporate taxes would "impart an added momentum to the growth process, create multiplier beneficial effects all around and also attract greater foreign investment."
